extra_vocab.en: a health problem where nuts make a person sick
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇留言裡指兩位賓客對堅果過敏，所以餐廳必須讓菜單避開堅果。with nut allergies 放在 guests 後面，說明是哪一種賓客；餐飲業很常在訂位時確認這類需求。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: allergy 的後面接 to（an allergy to nuts）；nut 在 nut allergies 裡是形容詞，不加 s，複數的 s 加在 allergies。

examples.en: Please tell the chef if any guest has a nut allergy.
examples.zh: 如果有任何賓客對堅果過敏，請告訴主廚。

examples.en: Several attendees listed nut allergies on the registration form.
examples.zh: 幾位出席者在報名表上填寫了堅果過敏。

examples.en: This dessert contains no nuts, so it is safe for people with nut allergies.
examples.zh: 這道甜點不含堅果，所以對堅果過敏的人也能安心食用。

examples.en: We chose a caterer that can handle nut allergies safely.
examples.zh: 我們選了一家能安全處理堅果過敏的外燴業者。

similar.diff: food allergies 泛指各種食物過敏；nut allergies 只指堅果。

example.en: The menu clearly marks dishes that may cause food allergies.
example.zh: 菜單上清楚標示了可能引起食物過敏的菜色。

similar.diff: dietary restrictions 範圍更廣，包含素食、宗教或健康因素的飲食限制，不一定是過敏。

example.en: Please let us know about any dietary restrictions before the event.
example.zh: 活動前請告知我們任何飲食限制。

confusable.diff: allergic 是形容詞，allergy 是名詞，兩者後面都接 to。
confusable.usage: 形容詞用 be allergic to nuts，名詞用 have an allergy to nuts 或 nut allergies，不要說 be allergy。

example.en: One of our guests is allergic to nuts, so please check the sauces.
example.zh: 我們的一位賓客對堅果過敏，所以請檢查一下醬料。

extra_vocab.en: a formal way to begin telling someone important information
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇留言裡，餐廳用它引出取消規定（48 小時內取消要收費）。語氣客氣但正式，提醒對方接下來的內容很重要，常見於公告、電子郵件與語音留言。
extra_vocab.pattern: Please be advised that + 子句
extra_vocab.grammar_note: be advised 是被動語態，後面接 that 子句；Please advise 是「請給我建議」，意思不同，不能互換。

examples.en: Please be advised that the office will close early on Friday.
examples.zh: 敬請注意，辦公室星期五會提早關閉。

examples.en: Please be advised that all invoices must be paid within thirty days.
examples.zh: 敬請注意，所有請款單都必須在三十天內付清。

examples.en: Please be advised that prices may change without prior notice.
examples.zh: 敬請注意，價格可能不另行通知而調整。

examples.en: Please be advised that your flight may be delayed because of weather.
examples.zh: 敬請注意，您的班機可能因天氣而延誤。

similar.diff: Please note that 更常見、語氣較輕；Please be advised that 更正式。

example.en: Please note that the meeting room is booked until noon.
example.zh: 請注意，會議室已被預約到中午。

similar.phrase: We would like to inform you that
similar.diff: 語氣同樣正式，但主詞是 we，比較像寫信或公告的開頭。

example.en: We would like to inform you that the shipment has arrived.
example.zh: 我們要通知您，貨物已經到了。

confusable.diff: advice 是名詞「建議」，advised 是動詞 advise 的過去分詞。
confusable.usage: advice 是不可數名詞，不加 s，發音 /ədˈvaɪs/；advise 是動詞，發音 /ədˈvaɪz/。

example.en: I would like your advice before we sign the contract.
example.zh: 簽約之前，我想聽聽你的建議。

extra_vocab.en: in a happy and willing way
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇留言裡，we will gladly accommodate 表示餐廳很樂意配合有過敏的賓客，語氣友善、有服務精神。gladly 放在 will 和動詞之間，是服務業常用的客氣說法。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: gladly 是副詞，通常放在助動詞與動詞之間（will gladly + V）；形容詞 glad 則用 be glad to + V。

example.en: We would gladly accept your invitation to the opening event.
example.zh: 我們很樂意接受您參加開幕活動的邀請。

example.en: Our staff will gladly help you choose the right plan.
example.zh: 我們的員工很樂意幫您選擇合適的方案。

example.en: The company will gladly provide references upon request.
example.zh: 公司樂意在需要時提供推薦人資料。

examples.en: Please call us anytime, and we will gladly answer your questions.
examples.zh: 歡迎隨時來電，我們很樂意回答您的問題。

examples.en: I would gladly attend the seminar if my schedule allows.
examples.zh: 如果行程允許，我很樂意參加這場研討會。

examples.en: The chef gladly changed the menu for our vegetarian guest.
examples.zh: 主廚欣然為我們的素食賓客更改了菜單。

examples.en: She gladly took on the extra project last month.
examples.zh: 她上個月欣然接下了額外的專案。

confusable.diff: glad 是形容詞，gladly 是副詞，詞性不同。
confusable.usage: glad 用在 be glad to + V 或 be glad that…；gladly 修飾動詞，如 will gladly help。

example.en: I am glad to confirm your booking for Friday evening.
example.zh: 我很高興確認您星期五晚上的訂位。

similar.diff: happily 也能表示樂意，但更常指「開心地」；gladly 更強調願意配合對方的要求。

example.en: The team happily agreed to move the meeting to Friday.
example.zh: 團隊欣然同意把會議改到星期五。

similar.diff: willingly 強調出於自願、不勉強；gladly 多了高興的語氣。

example.en: The staff willingly worked overtime to finish the order.
example.zh: 員工自願加班完成這筆訂單。

example.en: We are glad to inform you that your order has shipped.
example.zh: 我們很高興通知您，您的訂單已經出貨。

example.en: The client was pleased with the quick response from our team.
example.zh: 客戶對我們團隊的快速回應感到滿意。

example.en: We are delighted to welcome you to our new restaurant.
example.zh: 我們很高興歡迎您蒞臨我們的新餐廳。

example.en: Are you willing to work on the weekend for this project?
example.zh: 你願意為這個專案週末加班嗎？

extra_vocab.en: people who come to an event, a hotel, or a restaurant
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇留言裡，your party has grown from eight to twelve guests 是指晚宴的人數從八位增加到十二位，所以要換到包廂。餐廳與飯店常用 guests 來計算人數。

example.en: Please send me the final guest list by Thursday noon.
example.zh: 請在星期四中午前把最終的賓客名單寄給我。

example.en: Hotel guests can use the fitness center free of charge.
example.zh: 飯店房客可以免費使用健身中心。

example.en: A guest speaker from Tokyo will open the conference.
example.zh: 一位來自東京的特邀講者將為會議開場。

example.en: Only invited guests may enter the VIP lounge.
example.zh: 只有受邀賓客可以進入貴賓休息室。

examples.en: We expect about forty guests at the client dinner on Friday.
examples.zh: 我們預計星期五的客戶晚宴大約有四十位賓客。

examples.en: The hotel offers free breakfast to all guests.
examples.zh: 這間飯店提供所有房客免費早餐。

examples.en: Guests are asked to register at the front desk.
examples.zh: 請賓客在櫃檯登記。

examples.en: Thank you for informing us that two more guests will attend.
examples.zh: 謝謝您通知我們還會有兩位賓客出席。

confusable.diff: customer 是付錢購買商品或服務的顧客；guest 是被邀請或受招待的客人。

example.en: The store gave every customer a small gift with the purchase.
example.zh: 商店送給每位顧客一份小禮物作為購物贈品。

confusable.diff: visitor 是來訪的人，例如來公司拜訪；guest 強調被招待、住宿或用餐。

example.en: All visitors must sign in at the reception desk.
example.zh: 所有訪客都必須在接待櫃檯簽到。

similar.diff: attendee 專指出席會議、研討會等活動的人；guest 則強調被邀請或受招待。

example.en: Each attendee will receive a name tag and a program.
example.zh: 每位出席者都會拿到名牌和節目表。

example.en: Our host arranged a private dinner for the visiting clients.
example.zh: 我們的主辦人為來訪客戶安排了一場私人晚宴。

example.en: The hotel is known for its warm hospitality.
example.zh: 這間飯店以親切的款待聞名。

example.en: I would like to change my reservation from eight to twelve people.
example.zh: 我想把訂位人數從八人改成十二人。

example.en: Please reply to the invitation by the end of this week.
example.zh: 請在本週結束前回覆這份邀請。

senses.en: a person who is invited to an event or meal

example.en: Each guest at the dinner received a small gift from the company.
example.zh: 晚宴上的每位賓客都收到公司送的小禮物。

senses.en: a person who pays to stay in a hotel
senses.distinguish: 出現在飯店、住宿的情境時，指住房的客人。

example.en: The hotel asks every guest to leave the room key at the desk.
example.zh: 飯店要求每位房客把房間鑰匙留在櫃檯。

senses.en: a special person who joins a show or an event
senses.distinguish: 前面常有 special 或接 speaker，指被邀請來參與的嘉賓。

example.en: The special guest at the launch was a well-known chef.
example.zh: 這場發表會的特別來賓是一位知名主廚。

extra_vocab.en: depending on something that must happen first
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇留言裡，餐廳願意配合過敏賓客，但有一個條件：必須在週三中午前收到最終菜單。contingent upon 語氣很正式，常見於合約、通知與商務信件。
extra_vocab.pattern: 主要子句, contingent upon + 名詞／所有格 + V-ing
extra_vocab.grammar_note: contingent upon（也可寫 contingent on）後面接名詞或 V-ing，不接完整子句；要接子句時改用 provided that 或 depends on whether。

examples.en: The final payment is contingent upon the client's approval of the work.
examples.zh: 最後一筆款項要視客戶是否核准工作成果而定。

examples.en: Our offer is contingent upon receiving your signed contract by Monday.
examples.zh: 我們的報價以在星期一前收到您簽署的合約為條件。

examples.en: The promotion is contingent upon passing the annual performance review.
examples.zh: 這次升遷取決於是否通過年度績效考核。

examples.en: The outdoor event is contingent upon good weather on Saturday.
examples.zh: 戶外活動要視星期六的天氣是否良好而定。

similar.diff: depending on 較口語，後面也可接 whether 子句；contingent upon 更正式。

example.en: We will decide on the budget depending on next quarter's sales.
example.zh: 我們會視下一季的銷售狀況來決定預算。

similar.diff: subject to 常見於合約，意思是「須經…」或「受…約束」，語氣同樣正式。

example.en: All orders are subject to availability and final approval.
example.zh: 所有訂單都須視供貨情況及最終核准而定。

similar.diff: provided that 後面接完整子句，意思是「只要…就」。

example.en: We will ship the goods provided that payment is received.
example.zh: 只要收到款項，我們就會出貨。

confusable.diff: contingency 是名詞，指可能發生的意外或應變準備；contingent 是形容詞，意思是「視…而定」。

example.en: We set aside money as a contingency for unexpected costs.
example.zh: 我們預留一筆錢，以應付意外的費用。

extra_vocab.text: contingent upon our receiving the final menu selections no later than Wednesday noon.
extra_vocab.zh: 條件是我們必須在週三中午之前收到最終的菜單選擇。
extra_vocab.note: 這是原句後半的附加條件，語氣正式客氣，提醒對方要在期限前送出餐點選擇，餐廳才能配合過敏的需求。
extra_vocab.structure: contingent upon + 所有格 + V-ing + 受詞 + no later than + 時間

grammar.explain: contingent upon 是介系詞片語，後面接名詞或 V-ing，表示「以…為條件」，用來為前面的主要子句加上條件。
V-ing 前面的 our 表示收到的人是「我們」，這是較正式的寫法；口語也可說 us receiving。
表示最晚的期限，no later than Wednesday noon 就是「最晚週三中午」，含當時在內。

extra_vocab.pattern: （主要子句）, contingent upon + 所有格 + V-ing + N + no later than + 時間

paraphrase.en: but only if we receive the final menu selections by noon on Wednesday.
paraphrase.zh: 但前提是我們在週三中午前收到最終的菜單選擇。

paraphrase.en: provided that we receive the final menu selections by Wednesday at noon.
paraphrase.zh: 只要我們在週三中午前收到最終的菜單選擇。

examples.en: The discount is contingent upon our receiving full payment no later than May 30.
examples.zh: 這項折扣的條件是我們最晚在五月三十日前收到全額款項。

examples.en: Your reservation is contingent upon your confirming the guest count by Thursday.
examples.zh: 您的訂位須以您在星期四前確認賓客人數為條件。

extra_vocab.note: 這個字沒有直接出現在文章裡，但文章最後的 incur a fee（招致費用）拼法和發音都很像它，容易搞混。occur 是「發生」，incur 是「承擔（費用、損失）」，兩者要分清楚。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: occur 是不及物動詞，不能用被動，要說 The error occurred，不說 was occurred；變化時最後的 r 要重複，寫成 occurred、occurring。

example.en: A short delay occurs whenever the system updates its database.
example.zh: 每次系統更新資料庫時，都會出現短暫的延遲。

example.en: The error occurred while the staff were entering the orders.
example.zh: 員工在輸入訂單時發生了錯誤。

example.en: Please report any problems occurring during the installation.
example.zh: 安裝期間如有任何問題發生，請回報。

example.en: If any problems occur, please contact the IT hotline.
example.zh: 如果發生任何問題，請聯絡資訊部門專線。

example.en: Mistakes occur frequently when data is entered by hand.
example.zh: 用手輸入資料時，錯誤經常發生。

example.en: It never occurred to me that the invoice might be wrong.
example.zh: 我從沒想過這張請款單可能有錯。

examples.en: When did the system failure first occur during the test?
examples.zh: 系統故障在測試中是什麼時候第一次發生的？

examples.en: Coverage applies only to damage that occurs during transport.
examples.zh: 保障範圍只適用於運送過程中發生的損壞。

examples.en: Most accidents occur because workers skip the safety checks.
examples.zh: 大多數意外是因為工人省略安全檢查才發生。

confusable.diff: incur 是「招致、承擔」費用或損失；occur 是事情「發生」。
confusable.usage: incur 是及物動詞，後面接費用、損失等受詞（incur a fee）；occur 是不及物動詞，後面不接受詞。

example.en: The company may incur extra costs if the order is changed.
example.zh: 如果訂單被更改，公司可能要承擔額外的費用。

confusable.diff: occupy 是「佔用、佔據」場所或時間，發音和拼法都與 occur 相近，但意思不同。

example.en: The sales team occupies the entire third floor of the building.
example.zh: 業務團隊佔用了大樓的整個三樓。

similar.diff: happen 較口語、最通用；occur 比較正式，常用於報告與通知。

example.en: What happened to the shipment that was due on Monday?
example.zh: 星期一應該到的那批貨出了什麼狀況？

similar.diff: take place 用於預定的活動或會議，不用於意外；occur 兩者都可以。

example.en: The annual meeting will take place in the main hall.
example.zh: 年度會議將在大廳舉行。

similar.diff: arise 強調問題或情況「出現」，常和 problem、issue 搭配。

example.en: Problems may arise if the schedule changes at the last minute.
example.zh: 如果時程在最後一刻更動，可能會出現問題。

example.en: The incident was reported to the safety manager right away.
example.zh: 這起事件立刻被通報給安全經理。

example.en: We will look into the issue and call you back tomorrow.
example.zh: 我們會調查這個問題，明天回電給您。

example.en: The company holds a networking event every spring.
example.zh: 公司每年春天都會舉辦一場交流活動。

derived.link: occur + -rence（r 要多寫一個），變成名詞，像 prefer → preference、refer → reference
re-（再次）+ occur，像 rewrite、return，再發生一次

senses.en: to happen, often without a plan

example.en: A power failure occurred during the final test of the machine.
example.zh: 機器最後測試時發生了停電。

senses.distinguish: 後面常接 to + 人，主詞多半是 it 或 an idea，不是事件發生。

example.en: It occurred to the manager that the deadline was too tight.
example.zh: 經理突然想到這個期限太趕了。
